name: Gheg Albanian

ancestors.notes: Written with the same standard Albanian Latin alphabet as the Tosk-based literary standard; the two dialect groups share one orthography even though they diverge phonologically.

notes: Gheg Albanian, spoken north of the Shkumbin river (Kosovo, northern Albania, North Macedonia, Montenegro). Uses the same Latin alphabet and letter values as standard (Tosk-based) Albanian, so the grapheme table is inherited unchanged (graphemes_base=sq); the well-documented phonological differences are NOT orthographically marked and so cannot be expressed as distinct grapheme keys without violating AGENTS.md §2/§3: Gheg has phonemic vowel length and nasalization (26 vowel qualities: /a e i o u y/ each long/short, oral/nasal, none written distinctly), a central rounded /øː/ in northwestern dialects (written œ, not in the standard alphabet), and in Northeastern Gheg the palatal stops /c/, /ɡʲ/ realized as standard Albanian orthography surfaces as post-alveolar affricates [t͡ʃ], [d͡ʒ]. Common consonant-cluster assimilations (mb→m, ngj→nj, nd→n) are colloquial/dialectal, not part of the literary norm, so left unencoded (word_exceptions would be needed for a closed list, which is out of scope for a stub-to-basic spec).
